Task: kvlog-torn-tail
Editable paths (relative to the workspace root): server/

A small TCP key-value server (server/main.go) appends every PUT as a key=value line to data/kv.log, fsyncs the file and only then answers OK. On start it replays the log to rebuild its in-memory map. Under repeated crashes and restarts, including crashes in the middle of a disk write, a client that stored keys and was told OK later reads some of them back as NONE.

Observed on seed 1: the server was crashed and restarted 11 times (several of the crashes landed inside a disk operation, with torn writes enabled). At the end the client reported: acknowledged write lost: k151=v151, server now answers "NONE". The server never logged an error on startup.

Expected: every PUT that returned OK must be readable after any number of crashes and restarts.

Tools: list_files, read_file, write_file, edit_file for the workspace; run_seeds(seeds) to replay up to 4 seeds (integers from 0 to 1000; seed 1 reproduces the failure above) and see pass or fail with a reason and the end of the trace; submit() to finish.

content: The likely cause is in `open`: when the log ends in a torn partial line (no trailing newline), `parse` stops at the last complete line but the file is never truncated. The next PUT then appends after the torn bytes, so its record merges with the fragment and the acknowledged key is lost on the next replay. I'll truncate the torn tail on open and sync it before serving.

content:
I fixed the bug in `server/main.go`, and seeds 1–12 all pass, including seed 1 from the report.

**Cause:** On startup, `open` replays the log and stops at the last complete newline-terminated record. It never removed the torn partial record left by a crash mid-write. The next PUT then appended after those leftover bytes, so the new record was glued onto the fragment. On the following replay, that merged line was unparseable and the acknowledged key was lost, which is why the server reported `NONE` with no startup error.

**Fix:** In `open`, when `parse` reports that the file has bytes past the last complete record, the code now truncates the file to that offset and fsyncs before serving. New appends therefore start on a clean line boundary.

I haven't run the full hidden seed set, only these 12 seeds. I haven't changed anything else, and I didn't special-case any seed.
